questions.q: What is Yahweh about to take away from Jerusalem and Judah?
questions.a: Yahweh is about to take away their supply of bread and water and other support.

questions.q: What kind of leaders will Yahweh take away from his people?
questions.a: Yahweh will take away the warrior, judge, prophet, diviner, and elder.

questions.q: What other leaders and skilled workers will Yahweh take away?
questions.a: Yahweh will take away the military officers, important officials, advisors, skilled craftsmen, and magicians.

questions.q: Who will lead Judah and Jerusalem?
questions.a: Youths will lead them and the young will rule over them.

questions.q: Who will oppress the people?
questions.a: The people will be oppressed by each other and everyone by his neighbor.

questions.q: What will a man ask a relative who owns a coat to do?
questions.a: He will ask him to become their ruler, even though their community is in ruins.

questions.q: How will the relative respond to being asked to lead?
questions.a: He will refuse, saying he has no food or coat in his house, so he cannot be their leader.

questions.q: Why is Jerusalem ruined and Judah fallen?
questions.a: They are ruined and fallen because their speech and actions are against Yahweh.

questions.q: What witnesses against Judah and Jerusalem?
questions.a: The look on their faces witnesses against them.

questions.q: What will happen to the righteous?
questions.a: It will be well with the righteous.

questions.q: What will happen to the wicked?
questions.a: It will go badly for the wicked.

questions.q: Where do their leaders lead them?
questions.a: Their leaders lead them astray and confuse the direction of their path.

questions.q: What is Yahweh ready to do to the peoples?
questions.a: Yahweh is ready to judge them.

questions.q: What will Yahweh do to the elders and officials of his people?
questions.a: Yahweh will pronounce judgment on them.

questions.q: What does Yahweh accuse the leaders of doing to the poor?
questions.a: Yahweh accuses them of crushing his people and grinding the faces of the poor.

questions.q: What does Yahweh say about the women of Zion?
questions.a: Yahweh says they are proud, walk with their heads held high, flirt with their eyes, and jingle the bracelets on their ankles.

questions.q: What will the Lord, Yahweh do to the daughters of Zion?
questions.a: Yahweh will form diseased scabs on their heads and make them bald.

questions.q: What will Yahweh remove from the women of Zion?
questions.a: Yahweh will remove their anklets, headbands, and crescent necklaces.

questions.q: What other jewelry will Yahweh take away?
questions.a: He will take away their earrings, bracelets, and veils.

questions.q: What other items will Yahweh take away from the women?
questions.a: He will take away their headdresses, ankle chains, sashes, perfume containers, and charms.

questions.q: What kind of rings will Yahweh take away?
questions.a: He will take away their signet rings and nose rings.

questions.q: What clothing and items will Yahweh take away?
questions.a: He will take away their fine robes, capes, cloaks, and purses.

questions.q: What final items will Yahweh take away?
questions.a: He will take away their mirrors, linen garments, turbans, and veils.

questions.q: What will happen to replace the women’s fine things?
questions.a: Instead of perfume they will stink. Instead of fine sashes, they will have ropes. Instead of nice hair, they will be bald, and instead of beauty, they will have scars from branding.

questions.q: What will happen to the men?
questions.a: The men will fall by the sword.

questions.q: What will happen to the city’s gates and to Jerusalem?
questions.a: Her gates will mourn, the city will be emptied, and Jerusalem will sit on the ground like a desolate woman.

commentary.text: The calamities about to come upon the land. (Is. 3:1-9) The wickedness of the people. (Is. 3:10-15) The distress of the proud, luxurious women of Zion. (Is. 3:16-26)

Is. 3:1-9 God was about to deprive Judah of every stay and support. The city and the land were to be made desolate, because their words and works had been rebellious against the Lord; even at his holy temple. If men do not stay themselves upon God, he will soon remove all other supports, and then they must sink. Christ is the Bread of life and the Water of life; if he be our Stay, we shall find that is a good part not to be taken away, John 6:27. Here note, 1. That the condition of sinners is exceedingly woful. 2. It is the soul that is damaged by sin. 3. Whatever evil befals sinners, be sure that they bring it on themselves.

Is. 3:10-15 The rule was certain; however there might be national prosperity or trouble, it would be well with the righteous and ill with the wicked. Blessed be God, there is abundant encouragement to the righteous to trust in him, and for sinners to repent and return to him. It was time for the Lord to show his might. He will call men to a strict account for all the wealth and power intrusted to and abused by them. If it is sinful to disregard the necessities of the poor, how odious and wicked a part do they act, who bring men into poverty, and then oppress them!

Is. 3:16-26 The prophet reproves and warns the daughters of Zion of the sufferings coming upon them. Let them know that God notices the folly and vanity of proud women, even of their dress. The punishments threatened answered the sin. Loathsome diseases often are the just punishment of pride. It is not material to ask what sort of ornaments they wore; many of these things, if they had not been in fashion, would have been ridiculed then as now. Their fashions differed much from those of our times, but human nature is the same. Wasting time and money, to the neglect of piety, charity, and even of justice, displease the Lord. Many professors at the present day, seem to think there is no harm in worldly finery; but were it not a great evil, would the Holy Spirit have taught the prophet to expose it so fully? The Jews being overcome, Jerusalem would be levelled with the ground; which is represented under the idea of a desolate female seated upon the earth. And when the Romans had destroyed Jerusalem, they struck a medal, on which was represented a woman sitting on the ground in a posture of grief. If sin be harboured within the walls, lamentation and mourning are near the gates.
